reasoning: Classify 1..100 by residue mod 7. Since 100 = 14*7 + 2, residues 1 and 2 each occur 15 times; residues 0,3,4,5,6 each occur 14 times. Two distinct elements sum to a multiple of 7 iff their residues are complementary: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), or both are 0. So from each complementary pair we may take at most one residue class entirely, and at most one multiple of 7. Upper bound: max(15,14) + max(15,14) + max(14,14) + 1 = 15+15+14+1 = 45. Construction: all n ≡ 1 (mod 7): {1,8,...,99} (15 numbers); all n ≡ 2 (mod 7): {2,9,...,100} (15 numbers); all n ≡ 3 (mod 7): {3,10,...,94} (14 numbers); plus the single multiple of 7, namely 7. Any two distinct elements have residue sums in {2,3,4,5,6,1,2,3} (mod 7), never 0, so this 45-element set works and 45 is maximal.
